evals.prompt: I'm building an ASP.NET Core minimal API and want to load all parameters under /MyApp/prod from SSM Parameter Store into IConfiguration. How do I wire this up?
evals.expected_output: Adds the AWSSSM.Provider NuGet package and calls builder.Configuration.AddSsmParameters(...) with configurator options => options.Path = "/MyApp/prod", explaining the parameters become configuration keys by stripping the path prefix and converting slashes to colons (/MyApp/prod/Db/Host becomes Db:Host).
assertions: Uses AddSsmParameters (not AddSecretsManager) and the AWSSSM.Provider package
Sets Path to /MyApp/prod as the scoping mechanism
Explains the / to : key conversion and path-prefix stripping correctly

evals.prompt: I have parameters in SSM Parameter Store including some SecureString values, and I want the app to pick up changes every minute without restarting. What options do I need?
evals.expected_output: Sets PollingInterval = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(1) for background reload, keeps WithDecryption = true (the default) for SecureString values, and mentions the kms:Decrypt IAM permission requirement alongside ssm:GetParametersByPath.
assertions: Sets PollingInterval to enable background reload rather than suggesting a restart or manual reload call
Does not disable WithDecryption or claim SecureString needs extra package code
Mentions kms:Decrypt is required for SecureString decryption

evals.prompt: A parameter at /MyApp/Config contains JSON like {"ConnectionStrings":{"Primary":"..."}}. How do I read the Primary connection string from IConfiguration?
evals.expected_output: Explains the JSON value is recursively flattened using ':'-delimited keys, so with Path = /MyApp the value is readable at configuration["Config:ConnectionStrings:Primary"], and that key lookups are case-insensitive.
assertions: Correctly describes ':'-delimited JSON flattening with the path prefix stripped
States that configuration key lookups are case-insensitive
Does not claim Newtonsoft/JSON.NET or a different delimiter is used

evals.prompt: I called AddSsmParameters() with the default options but my parameter /Prod/ApiKey isn't showing up and nothing throws. Why?
evals.expected_output: Explains the default Path is "/", so the parameter should appear under Prod:ApiKey (leading slash stripped, slash to colon) — and lists likely causes: an IAM identity without ssm:GetParametersByPath permission for the hierarchy, the parameter living in a different region than the client resolved, or a ParameterFilter excluding it. Also notes this package never throws for absent parameters — an empty path yields an empty configuration.
assertions: Correctly maps /Prod/ApiKey under the default root Path to the key Prod:ApiKey
Does not invent an IgnoreMissingValues-style error, or claim the provider throws when a parameter is absent
Lists permission, region, or filter mismatch as candidate causes

evals.prompt: For local development I want to point the SSM provider at a Floci container on localhost:4566 instead of real AWS.
evals.expected_output: Uses ConfigureSsmConfig to set ServiceURL = http://localhost:4566 (and AuthenticationRegion), passes BasicAWSCredentials("test", "test") or similar non-empty dummy credentials, and notes Floci fully emulates Parameter Store including SecureString decryption.
assertions: Uses ConfigureSsmConfig with ServiceURL pointed at the local endpoint rather than CreateClient bypassing it unnecessarily
Uses non-empty dummy credentials for the local emulator
Does not invent a dedicated first-class Floci/LocalStack integration package

evals.prompt: Is AWSSSM.Provider the same as AWSSecretsManager.Provider? Can I use AddSecretsManager to read SSM parameters?
evals.expected_output: Clarifies they are sibling packages for different AWS services: AWSSSM.Provider reads SSM Parameter Store via AddSsmParameters/GetParametersByPath; AWSSecretsManager.Provider reads Secrets Manager via AddSecretsManager. AddSecretsManager cannot read SSM parameters, and the options types are different (SsmConfigurationProviderOptions has no UseBatchFetch/IgnoreMissingValues/AcceptedSecretArns; the SSM interface is IAmazonSimpleSystemsManagement).
assertions: Clearly separates the two packages and their AWS services
States AddSecretsManager does not read SSM Parameter Store
Does not claim SsmConfigurationProviderOptions has UseBatchFetch, IgnoreMissingValues, or AcceptedSecretArns options
